events.title: Battle of Bannockburn Concludes
events.description: On the second day of the battle, Scottish forces led by Robert the Bruce decisively defeated the larger English army of King Edward II near Stirling, Scotland.
events.significance: The victory secured de facto Scottish independence and strengthened Robert the Bruce's position as king, leading to formal English recognition of Scottish sovereignty in the 1328 Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton.

events.title: John Cabot Reputedly Lands in North America
events.description: According to traditional accounts, Italian navigator John Cabot, sailing under commission from King Henry VII of England, sighted and landed on the North American coast, likely in Newfoundland or Cape Breton.
events.significance: The voyage laid the foundation for English claims to North America and later British colonization of the continent.

events.title: Napoleon's Grande Armée Crosses the Niemen River
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte led a force of more than 400,000 men across the Niemen River into Russian territory, beginning the French invasion of Russia.
events.significance: The campaign ended in catastrophic losses for France and marked a turning point in the Napoleonic Wars, contributing to Napoleon's eventual downfall.

events.title: Soviet Blockade of West Berlin Begins
events.description: The Soviet Union halted road, rail, and barge traffic between West Germany and the Western-controlled sectors of Berlin, prompting the Western Allies to organize the Berlin Airlift.
events.significance: It was one of the first major crises of the Cold War and led to the supply of West Berlin by air for nearly a year, strengthening Western unity and contributing to the creation of NATO and the division of Germany.

events.title: U.S. Supreme Court Overturns Roe v. Wade
events.description: In Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, the Supreme Court ruled that the Constitution does not confer a right to abortion, overturning Roe v. Wade (1973) and Planned Parenthood v. Casey (1992).
events.significance: The decision returned abortion regulation to individual states and reshaped American law, politics, and healthcare access.
